newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAK TELECOM TO MANDATE CITIBANK FOR SYND LOAN.
newsitem.headline: SLOVAK TELECOM TO MANDATE CITIBANK FOR SYND LOAN.

text.p: The Slovak state-owned telecom monopoly Slovenske Telekomunikacie s.p. (ST) on Monday said it planned a $100 million syndicated loan with Citibank by the end of this year.
"ST will sign a $100 million syndicated loan with Citibank once transformation into a 100 percent state-owned joint-stock company is completed," ST spokesman Lubomir Stancel told Reuters.
The loan would carry an interest rate of 6.5 percent, but Stancel declined to comment on the maturity of the credit.
Stancel said the transformation of ST in a joint-stock company would require an amendment to the law on strategic companies scheduled to be approved by the Slovak parliament by the end of this year.

The loan is to finance part of ST's ambitious modernisation project, to be completed in 2000, of upgrading the Slovak telecom network to EU standards. Overall investment into the project is expected to total around 55 billion crowns.

Transformation of ST into a joint-stock company is the first step towards partial privatisation, planned for 1998. By the end of September, British consultant N.M. Rothschild Investment Bank is to present a proposal on the optimum mode of entry of foreign capital into ST. -- Peter Laca, Bratislava Newsroom, 42-7-210-3687
